column1: # deps.tsv -- every external command this setup depends on, and what installs it.
# tree-sitter-cli was missing from install.sh for as long as install.sh has
# existed, and nothing said so. It could not: nothing in this repository names
# it. The neovim config is a separate repository, cloned by `install.sh --nvim`,
# and nvim-treesitter shells out to `tree-sitter` to build a parser. So the
# dependency was real, the machine it was developed on had it, and a fresh
# machine got a neovim that silently could not build parsers.
# A scan of this repository cannot find a dependency this repository does not
# mention. A hand-written list can, and this is it. `noct-check deps` checks it
#   1. every command here is installed by install.sh, in the list named
#   2. every command here is actually present on this machine
#   3. every `command -v X` and `need X` guard in bin/ and tests/ appears here
# (3) is what stops this file rotting: add a guard for a new tool and the suite
# fails until the tool is written down, with a package and a reason.
# Format: command <TAB> package <TAB> install.sh list <TAB> scope <TAB> why
#   list    the PKGS_* array in install.sh that must name the package, or "-"
#           for things that come with the base system and are never installed
#   scope   core      the setup is broken without it, and the check fails
#           optional  a machine may legitimately not have it (the four
#                     browsers, the tools only the test suite needs), and the
